chapter_title: The Three Earths that Exist, they bear Fruit.
spiritual_reading:
¶1
The chapter opens with “three earths” being “toiled over” and then yielding “good fruit.” In correspondence, **earth/field/ground** is the **natural mind as a receptacle**—the plane where seeds (interior truths in potency) can be received and brought to ultimate use. “Toil” and “farming” signify the ordered operations by which higher things are brought into ultimates: instruction, discipline, temptations, and the patient rearrangement of the natural so it can receive influx. “Fruit” is the **good of life**—uses and loves made actual in the outermost degree.

Spiritually, the statement that there are **three earths** describes **discrete degrees**: three distinct recipient planes in which the Divine can be terminated as effect. The movement is: at first the “earth” is resistant and must be worked (the natural not yet compliant), afterward it yields fruit (the natural made obedient, producing good in act). This establishes the law of regeneration: **influx from within requires preparation of the recipient**, and the sign of genuine reception is fruit.

¶2
The first earth is named: “this great earth that people are living upon.” This is the **outermost natural degree**, the sensate and civil life where truth must be embodied. The detailed implements define the correspondences of reformation in ultimates:
- **Ploughing**: opening and ordering the natural mind so that truths can enter in series.
- **Iron hoes**: **hard, natural truth** and external discipline (iron = truth in the lowest degree, strong and corrective) used to break up what is compacted and resistant.
- **Furrows**: the **structured receptacles** in the natural where seeds can be placed—ordered memory-knowledges and habits that can receive higher influx.
- **Turning over the soil**: inversion and rearrangement of priorities in the natural—bringing hidden evils to the surface and burying what is merely superficial, so the inner can govern the outer.
- **Harvest**: the bringing forth of uses into the world; the final confirmation that influx has reached its ultimate.

Thus this paragraph is the description of regeneration as it appears in the **natural plane**: the person, by means of external truths and disciplines, cooperates in preparing the outer mind. The spiritual motion is from **resistance → cultivation → fruit**, i.e., from a natural that does not yet correspond to heaven into a natural that does.

¶3
The second “field” is no longer external ground but “the living soul, the holy one,” spread “through the entire zone, above and below.” Here the correspondence shifts from the earth as literal world to the earth as an **inner recipient**: the “living soul” is the **intermediate living plane** where the natural and spiritual communicate—what Swedenborg would call the **spiritual degree of the person as it is present within the natural**, diffused “above and below” because it can be touched by higher influx and also act into lower forms.

Its “farmers” are “these two great light-givers, which journey through the heavens.” **Light-givers** correspond to the sources of illumination: **love and wisdom** in their appearing forms, or (in created representatives) the **sun and moon**—the governing principles that rule states. Their “journey through the heavens” signifies the orderly alternations and progressions of spiritual state by which influx is provided according to reception. In this context they are not mere physical luminaries but the **heavenly agencies of enlightenment**: one giving the fire within light (love as the source), the other giving reflected light (truth/faith as form).

They “toil and cultivate it, so that they will draw it towards their aspect.” To be drawn toward their “aspect” is to be brought into **correspondence with heaven’s form**—to have the inner life turned so it faces (receives) the ruling love and the ruling truth. This is the distinctively **spiritual work**: not merely rearranging external behavior, but changing the inner orientation of reception.

Then “it leaps up and comes to the heights.” **Leaping up** describes the **quickening** that occurs when the inner recipient is touched by genuine influx—life rising because it is being freed from what weighs it down. “Heights” correspond to **elevated spiritual states** (nearer to the source of influx). “It goes upwards, out from every place wherein it is” indicates that this living soul is gathered from dispersion in lower concerns and lifted into a more unified, higher order.

Finally, “it adds to them.” What is lifted up does not abandon the lower; rather, by discrete degrees, it **increases and perfects** the heavens (and the person’s higher states) by supplying what they can receive from below as ultimates made living—confirmations, uses, and a fuller termination. The movement here is the inverse of the natural paragraph: having been cultivated by heavenly light, the inner life **ascends**, and by ascending it **enriches** the higher forms it joins.

CONTINUOUS SPIRITUAL NARRATIVE
The chapter as a whole describes the Divine work of cultivation across **discrete degrees of reception**. There are “three earths” because there are distinct planes where life must be terminated: an outer earth (natural life), an inner field (the living soul diffused through the whole person), and—implied by the triad—an inmost recipient beyond what is yet described. First the doctrine is established: every recipient begins resistant and must be worked; the proof of successful influx is **fruit**, the good of life in ultimates.

The first earth shows reformation in the **natural degree**: by hard, external truths (iron) and ordered disciplines (ploughing, furrows, turning), the natural mind is opened and rearranged so that it can receive what is higher and bring it to harvest as uses. The second field shows regeneration in the **spiritual degree**: the living soul, present throughout the person, is acted upon by the two heavenly light-givers—love and truth in their governing function—whose orderly progression provides changing illumination. Under that influx, the inner life is drawn into the aspect of heaven, becomes vivified, rises into higher states, and by that ascent adds to the higher—perfecting the whole by bringing life into correspondence from within to without. In this way the text narrates one operation: **influx descends to cultivate the lower, and the cultivated lower then rises to conjoin and enrich the higher**, until fruit appears in the ultimate earth.

fills.notes: The law stated is: a field first resists influx and must be worked; only afterward does it yield fruit. The missing predicate should express initial non-reception/sterility before cultivation, in an impersonal cosmological register (not moral exhortation).

The sequence of correspondences is implement → breaking/opening → ordering into receptacles. After “They are ploughing in it …, it with iron hoes,” the simplest required tool is the plough, matching the operation of opening the outermost earth for seed/truth.

After furrows and turning-over comes the placement of seed into the prepared receptacles; correspondentially this is the insertion of truths into ordered memory-forms so that fruit (uses) can later be harvested. This also bridges naturally to the next clause “Afterwards they harvest fruit from it…”.

assessment: Most gaps are constrained by the farming-series correspondence (opening → breaking → furrowing → turning → sowing → harvest). Exact verb choices in ¶1 #1 and ¶2 #1 remain somewhat flexible, but the required spiritual functions (initial non-reception; plough as opening tool) are tight enough to restore with moderate confidence.
